cards.text: The prophet Jeremiah gets a word from the LORD. God tells him to listen to the words of this covenant and tell them to the men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem. That's a WHOLE lot of people to tell, friend, and Jeremiah doesn't even get a group chat.

cards.question: God's message starts strong. Cursed is the man who does not ___ the words of this covenant.

cards.text: This covenant isn't new. God commanded it to their forefathers when He brought them out of Egypt, which He calls the iron furnace, and friend, I've stood next to ovens my whole life, and even I'd hand in my apron for that one.

cards.question: When God brought Judah's forefathers out of Egypt, what did He say would happen if they obeyed Him?

answers.text: They would be His people and He their God
They would never lose a single battle again
They would rule over every nation on earth

cards.text: God says all of this was to establish an oath He swore to their forefathers.

cards.question: God swore an oath to Judah's forefathers to give them a land flowing with milk and honey.

cards.text: Then Jeremiah answers the LORD Himself: "Amen, LORD." No pressure.

Then the LORD tells Jeremiah to proclaim it in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem: hear the words of this covenant and carry them out. Hearing AND doing, friend: anybody can hear an alarm, but getting up is the hard part.

cards.question: From the time God brought Judah's fathers out of Egypt until today, He warned them to obey His voice only once.
Judah's fathers would not obey God or incline their ears to Him. What did each one follow instead?

answers.text: The stubbornness of his evil heart
The advice of the foreign kings
The teaching of the false prophets

cards.question: Because Judah's fathers did not keep the covenant, God brought on them all of its curses.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Jeremiah there's a conspiracy among the men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem. The only conspiracy in my old junk drawer was the rubber bands I shared it with, plotting who could stretch the farthest.

cards.question: God says the people of Judah and Jerusalem have returned to the sins of their forefathers.

cards.text: God says they have followed other gods to serve them.

cards.question: God says the covenant He made with His people's fathers has been broken. Who does He say broke it?

answers.text: The house of Israel and the house of Judah

cards.text: So the LORD says He's about to bring a disaster on them that they cannot escape. They will cry out to Him, but He will not listen.

cards.question: With the LORD not listening, where will the cities of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem go to cry out?

answers.text: To the gods they burn incense to
To the king of Egypt for help
To the priests at the temple

cards.question: The gods Judah has been burning incense to will save them in their time of disaster.

cards.text: God says Judah's gods are as numerous as its cities, and the altars to burn incense to Baal, a false god, are as many as the streets of Jerusalem. That's not a shrine, friend, that's a FRANCHISE, with a location on every corner.

cards.question: God tells Jeremiah to pray for the people of Judah and Jerusalem.

cards.text: God says He will not be listening when they call out to Him in their time of disaster. Then He asks, "What right has My beloved in My house, having carried out so many evil schemes? Can consecrated meat avert your doom?"

cards.question: God says that when the people are wicked, they rejoice.

cards.text: Then God paints a picture: the LORD once called them a flourishing olive tree, beautiful with well-formed fruit. Friend, I've stamped cookies for years and NEVER got a review that good.

cards.question: The LORD once called His people a flourishing olive tree. With a mighty roar, what will He do to that tree?
God says the LORD of Hosts, who ___ the people He called an olive tree, has decreed disaster against them.

cards.text: And God says why: the evil the house of Israel and the house of Judah have brought on themselves, provoking Him to anger by burning incense to Baal.
